principles: Truth-first status tables must describe implemented evidence, not desired future capability.
Completed local CLI behavior may be marked with ✅ only when source or smoke evidence exists.
Partial, unavailable, retired, future, and read-only diagnostic boundaries must remain explicit.
Document cleanup must not create or imply new lifecycle, production, or external proof authority.
drivers: Three documents currently mix implemented rows with partial/future/non-goal rows.
The user needs accurate tables to decide which future work to prioritize.
This high-risk process documentation touches lifecycle/proof vocabulary and must avoid overclaiming.

options.name: A: Minimal status-table correction only
pros: Fixes the real stale/ambiguous document problem
Keeps scope to the three approved documents
Avoids arbitrary runtime or gate implementation
cons: Does not add new hard automation
Some future work remains explicitly open

options.name: B: Implement all partial/future runtime capabilities now
pros: Could reduce future manual follow-up if every future row were truly desired
cons: Violates the no arbitrary optimization rule
Would re-open retired/non-goal rows such as ledger or server-backed proof
Much higher blast radius than the user asked for

options.name: C: Leave documents unchanged and only explain in chat
cons: Does not fix the stale plan-only and ambiguous status tables
Future agents would keep rediscovering the same inconsistency

rationale: Choose the narrow document correctness fix because the real issue is stale or ambiguous status representation, not missing runtime automation.

preMortem.scenario: The table marks a partial capability as fully complete
preMortem.trigger: Using ✅ without boundary text for diagnostic-only or unavailable rows
preMortem.consequence: Future agents or users overclaim hard gate or production behavior
preMortem.mitigation: Use ✅ only for implemented rows and keep ⚠️/🚫 rows explicit

preMortem.scenario: The patch reintroduces server-backed receipt proof language after retirement
preMortem.trigger: Copying old Authority-facing wording without retirement note
preMortem.consequence: Document contradicts the current product direction
preMortem.mitigation: Use external/retired boundary wording and keep local CLI non-authority claims separate

preMortem.scenario: The work becomes a code feature instead of docs cleanup
preMortem.trigger: Trying to implement partial/future rows while editing the documents
preMortem.consequence: Scope expands and risk increases unnecessarily
preMortem.mitigation: Keep code read-only for verification; open a new story for any real code correctness gap
